I farm cassava and cocoyam on this plot like my mother did before me. I cannot read, and I have no money to waste on bag fertilizer for tubers — my neighbors here in the South South do not put chemical on cassava, only maybe on yam if they have money. I will use the cuttings I saved from last harvest and put the goat droppings and household ash I gathered. The ground here gets plenty of rain, so I do not need to carry water, and I will work it myself with help from my daughter, hiring only a few hands to help clear and mound the ridges.
